brief.question: What does suno.com offer, how is its product organised, and what does a private, original prompt-to-song app (MusicMake) need in order to cover the same kinds of jobs?
brief.purpose: Learning, to design and build a private, non-commercial music maker. Not a clone.
constraints: Clean room for suno.com: public pages read by hand; no page source, scripts, network traffic or APIs
No automated capture, crawling or scraping of suno.com (its Terms forbid robots and scraping)
No Suno names, logos, text, audio or look-alike layout in MusicMake
Deep mode is used only to open our own notes in research/sources
brief.done_when: docs/suno-analysis.md and docs/musicmake-spec.md are written, and MusicMake's first version covers prompt to song, lyrics, takes, extend, remix, stems and export.

hypotheses.claim: Generating two takes per prompt lets people pick the better one, which hides the variance of generative models.
hypotheses.prediction: Each create action shows two results to choose from.

hypotheses.claim: A local open model (ACE-Step 1.5) plus Demucs covers the core jobs for a private app.
hypotheses.prediction: ACE-Step 1.5 offers text2music, cover (remix) and repaint (extend); Demucs gives 4 stems.

findings.statement: The core job is one prompt in, a complete song with vocals, lyrics and production out; everything else (Studio, Voices, Remix, Stems, Custom Models) builds on a generated or uploaded track.
User controls named publicly are: style, things to leave out, vocal gender, an adventurousness-type slider and a style-influence slider, plus a simple prompt-only mode.
The Terms forbid reverse engineering, scraping, robots and building competing products, so only public, hand-read information is used and nothing is automated against suno.com.
ACE-Step 1.5 (MIT) covers text-to-song with vocals, remix (cover) and extend (repaint) through a local REST API on under 4 GB of VRAM; Demucs (MIT) covers stem splitting.
For a private app, the jobs worth covering first are: prompt to song, lyrics to song, two takes, extend, remix, stems, download, library with favourites, and a lyric helper.

handoff: Research and MVP are done. Next: (1) the owner captures Suno screens by hand at 3 widths, adds them to research/screenshots/ (git-ignored) and records findings per screen; (2) run ACE-Step 1.5 on a GPU and compare vocals against YuE/DiffRhythm; (3) answer the open questions. Trap: don't point web_site_capture, web_walkthrough_record or any Deep tool at suno.com.
